steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Line cupcake pans with 18 paper liners.

Beat cream cheese and 1 cup sugar in a large bowl until well combined. Add eggs one at a time, mixing well after each addition. Stir in 1 teaspoon vanilla. Spoon batter into the prepared cupcake pans, 2/3 to 3/4 full.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, about 30 minutes. Remove from the oven and cool for 5 to 10 minutes.
Whisk sour cream, remaining 1 cup sugar, and remaining 1 teaspoon vanilla in a medium bowl until smooth. Spoon into the well on the top of each cupcake.
Return to the oven and bake until set, 5 to 7 more minutes. Place the pans on wire racks to cool. Do not remove cupcakes from the pans until completely cool.

raw_recipe.headline: Cheesecake Cupcakes
raw_recipe.description: These mini cheesecake cupcakes have a creamy sour cream topping—add an optional spoonful of your favorite pie filling for a finishing touch.

review.reviewBody: These mini cheesecakes were an immediate hit. I also used the standard 1 egg per brick of cream cheese rule and they turned out great. I also made the sour cream topping early and refridgerated it so it would thicken as per another reviewer.

I could see the potential of this recipe but I also had to tweak it. It called for way too much sugar. You only need 1/3 cup of sugar and one egg per 8oz block of cream cheese . I added 1/2 cup of sour cream and a couple teaspoons of lemon juice. As for the topping. I made it ahead and again the recipe calls for way too much sugar. I used a couple Tablespoons of sugar and 2 teaspoons of lemon juice. I baked them for 15 minutes BEFORE I spread the sour cream topping on them (carefully) then turned the oven off and left them in for another 7 minutes. . They turned out perfect.

Tried this, good basic recipe, but here are my alterations:
I used 32oz cream cheese (4 packs)
1 cup sour cream
3 eggs, 1 yolk
1/4 cup flour
1 tablespoon pure vanilla extract
1 teaspoon nutmeg
1.5 teaspoon lemon zest

I did use a graham cracker crust and baked it beforehand. I let oven cool, and baked @ 225 degrees for 3 hours and 40 mins with a water bath. Yes it's a long time, but cheesecake shouldn't be baked at high temps and in my experience, 350 or above caused cracks and sinks. It came out perfect!! I am topping with strawberry topping from the can, bc I won't have time to make it from scratch.
I scaled down this recipe .used 1-8 oz cheese 1/3 cup of sugar &2 eggs & it turned out great ,topped it with microwave lemon curd & fresh strawberries ,was a big hit with my celiac son

My mom has been making these since I was a little girl. She’s always used the 5 eggs and I think it’s delicious. When we add the sour cream mixture to the top we also add the pie filling and then put it back in the oven. The only difference she does is 1/4 cup sugar in the sour cream mixture and baked at 325 for 40 minutes.

Very tasty and easy gluten-free dessert. I substituted yogurt for the sour cream-make sure you do not use low-fat yogurt (like I did), as it'll take much longer for topping to set. I added fresh blueberries as a topping, and added apricot jam to glaze the fruit. I warmed/strained the jam and topped the blueberries with the glaze. It was a hit and will make again! We only had another couple for dinner, so I adjusted the recipe to make only 6 mini cheesecakes (1 block of cream cheese).

Great basic recipe but I made a few changes. Like other users had suggested, I used 3 eggs instead of 5. I also added a crust to the bottom of my cupcakes using 1 cup crushed chocolate Teddy Grahams, 3 tablespoons sugar, and 1/4 cup melted butter (mix together, sprinkle in each cupcake liner, then gently press down.) I then spooned the cream cheese mixture on top of my crust. I did not make the sour cream topping. Instead I sprinkled chocolate chips on top of each cupcake. I baked them for 25 mins and they came out perfect. Everyone at work loved them!!

Reliable recipe. Actually made it with some adjustments. I was worried they would be a bit runny so I put an oreo in the bottom of each one and poured the batter over. This let me make closer to 23 cupcakes.
I used about half of the recommended amount of sugar in the cupcake topping which was fine.
Also, noted that they came out much better in a my highest quality baking tin - so invest on good tins to make these for the best effect.

Liked it with changes. Per most of the other reviewers one egg per 8 ounces of cream cheese is plenty. If you drop a vanilla wafer in the bottom of the parchment cupcake cup you get a quick and easy crust. 1 cup of sugar for 1 cup of sour cream is ridiculous - I cut it down to 1/2 cup but I believe it could be cut down to 1/4 cup. I actually got 23 cup cakes out of the recipe which was nice. Baking time seems about right although I added a couple minutes to the second baking after the addition of the sour cream, which made it a total of 9 minutes. I also turned my oven up to 400 for those nine minutes as opening the door twice to pull them and put them back in dropped my temperature fairly significantly.

I have used this recipe in the past and am pretty sure it was edited from the original so these changes took it back to what it used to be.

I made these while I was testing different cheesecake recipes for my boyfriend's birthday and they were amazing! I added a thin graham cracker crust- just crushed graham cracker with melted butter- and it really helped balance it out. The only issue I had was how much excess batter I had, but that can easily be adjusted. After they baked I put them in the refrigerator to cool (I'm impatient!) and it helped them set up a lot. For someone who's need made a cheesecake before, I had absolutely no issues with them! Everyone loved them! I would 100% recommend this recipe!

I thought these turned out well, but definitely just use 3 eggs, and let the sour cream mixture chill for at least 10 minutes beforehand. After adding the sour cream mixture to the cupcakes, I baked them for close to 20 minutes to get it to set. It came out a bit like a meringue. :)

Love this recipe, used 3 eggs as suggested and had to cook a bit longer for sour cream to set. I used very thick sour cream. Also, I added extra flavour to some- hersheys choc syrup in some of the batter, caramel in others, Oreo cookies on the bottoms of some. Everyone always returns for more. Thank you!

WARNING: You may become addicted! My college roommate and I discovered this recipe for the first time during a night in - we were both shook! Since then I've made them for family functions, work events and significant others and they are an absolute HIT every time :) I'm not super into sweets but even for me it's impossible to eat just one. I always dice up some fresh strawberries as a topping after they come out the oven!
I make these all the time. They are always a hit. I usually put blueberries on top.

Definitely use one egg per block of cream cheese!!! Why the recipe calls for five eggs is absurd... If you use a graham cracker crust on the bottom, the batch will make 24. I added key lime to taste to one batch and cocoa powder (again, to taste) for an event and they turned out absolutely perfect. The one advice for if you are going to add things to taste, do it to where it is slightly overpowering. I thought the key lime batter tasted great while I was mixing but once they were backed, the lime was not very prevalent. Don't be too concerned if they "deflate" and have a cup/indent. I did not use the sour cream topping for either batch. I zested a lime to top of the key lime ones and confectioner's sugar for the chocolate. This was the first time I ever made cheesecake cups, I typically make a full cheesecake and I am extremely happy with the outcome.
I loved how they turned out, but they were a bit light on the inside and slightly overcooked on the bottom. Also, there was enough "batter" to make 20, not just 18.
Amazing but you can half the recipe for the icing
This recipe was awesome. I put a little jelly on top of each one to give a little color. My oven works better than most so the first cooming time needed to be reduced the second time around.

I made this as a gluten free desert option for my husband and I who are very envious of those who can eat cheesecake. This is cheese cake. I will make this again and again. I made some homemade jam to put on top with blueberries and blackberries. So good. I took them to a worksgiving party and everyone loved them and could not believe they were gluten free.
